name: Simple Partnership: Capital and Profit Shares
description: Share profit or loss when all partners keep their money invested for the same length of time.
script_scope: Teach the central simple-partnership idea: when every partner stays for the same time, time cancels and profit or loss follows the capital ratio. Build from two partners to three, including fractional parts of total capital, linked statements such as A invests three times B, finding one share from total profit, finding total profit from one partner's share, and reversing a known profit ratio back to the capital ratio. Include loss-sharing as the same ratio rule. Keep the learner focused on 'same time -> compare money only', simplify ratios early, and verify that all shares add back to the stated total.

name: Capital × Time: Joining and Leaving
description: Use money-time points when partners enter or leave a business at different times.
script_scope: Teach compound partnership through the book's equivalent-capital idea: profit share is proportional to capital multiplied by the number of months it remains invested. Introduce capital-months as earning points, then cover late joining, early leaving, different start dates, equal-profit cases created by different money/time combinations, and three-partner timelines. Make learners translate 'joins after 4 months' into 'invested for 8 months' in a one-year business. Use fresh exam-style share and ratio questions and check that the time window is counted from the start of the business, not from the date mentioned.

name: Changing Capital During the Partnership
description: Break the timeline into stages when a partner adds to or withdraws part of the investment.
script_scope: Teach piecewise capital-time accounting for partners whose capital changes while the business continues. Cover a withdrawal after some months, an additional investment, several partners changing at the same milestone, percentage increases such as a 50% increase in capital, two-stage and three-stage timelines, and multi-year versions. Emphasize that each stage contributes capital × months and the partner's total earning weight is the sum of those stage products. Prepare learners for objective patterns with additions, partial withdrawals and complete withdrawals.

name: Reverse Partnership: Find the Missing Capital or Time
description: Work backward from profit shares to recover an unknown investment, duration, or joining month.
script_scope: Teach the reverse use of profit ∝ capital × time. Given profit ratio and known times, divide out time to recover the capital ratio; given capitals, divide out capital to recover time. Include unknown joining month, unknown investment amount, equal-profit conditions, one known partner share, and clean algebraic cases where a profit difference fixes an unknown capital. End with a multi-stage reverse problem in the style of the chapter's later objective questions, while keeping every intermediate meaning explicit.

name: Working Partners and Special Profit Rules
description: Handle manager commission, charity, equal portions, and other deductions before the remaining profit is shared.
script_scope: Teach working-partner questions as a two-layer distribution: first remove any manager's commission, charity, equal portion or other stated special allocation; then divide only the remaining profit by the relevant capital or capital-time ratio. Cover a working partner who also receives an ordinary capital share, charity before distribution, part of profit split equally and the rest by capital, and interest-on-capital style splits from the objective exercise. Make the order of operations explicit so the special amount is never accidentally divided again.

name: Shared Rent and Usage Partnerships
description: Apply the partnership idea to rent or shared costs using usage × time, including unequal consumers.
script_scope: Generalize the chapter's pasture, house-rent and usage examples. For equal users, share cost by time used; for several animals or units, share by number × time; when different kinds consume at different rates, convert them to one common unit before multiplying by time. Include total rent from one person's share, staged house occupancy when people leave at different times, and reverse questions that infer missing usage or time from a rent share. Keep the model as 'cost follows consumption-time'.

name: Multi-Partner Algebra and Complex Investment Relations
description: Solve harder partnership puzzles with linked capital relations, totals, staged changes, and multi-year investments.
script_scope: Prepare learners for the chapter's harder algebraic partnership questions. Cover linked capital statements, total-capital constraints, recovering individual investments from profit shares, later additions and withdrawals that determine an initial capital, percentage changes to capital, and multi-year entry patterns. Teach learners to translate every sentence into either a capital relation or a capital-time expression before solving. Use a final capstone that combines a relation, a timeline change and a known profit ratio.

name: Data Sufficiency for Partnership
description: Decide whether the given statements are enough to determine a partnership answer uniquely.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's dedicated partnership data-sufficiency exercise. Distinguish calculating a useful ratio from having enough information to answer the exact question. Cover: both statements needed, statement I alone, statement II alone, either statement alone, even both insufficient, three-statement questions where any two suffice, cases where all three are required, and cases where all statements still leave a missing total or capital. Stress uniqueness: a statement set is sufficient only if it forces one answer.
